judgement.reason: It speaks to anxiety about election, not to someone who cannot believe in Jesus.
It is Zwingli's rule of correction by Scripture, not about Jesus's divine status or the Father and Spirit.
It shows the council deciding after public argument, with an eyewitness account as evidence.
It speaks of who joins pastors in discipline, not of settling doctrine.
It shows Zwingli accepting correction only from Scripture and says nothing about God's character or nature.
It speaks to anxiety about election, not to struggling to believe or being received.
It shows how Zwingli bound himself to Scripture, not what a modern reader misses.
Zwingli says he will be taught only from Scripture, which answers whether Scripture was the sole authority.
It shows the council ruling on Scripture's test, which bears on authority but does not directly say whether there were other authorities.
It says how Geneva's governors, lay elders chosen from the people, share discipline with pastors.
It shows who joined in censure but does not answer how the community responded when it failed someone.

It says who joins the pastors in discipline, not what members gave up.
It is Zwingli's doctrine of the Mass and says nothing about how reliable an outside record is.
